q: check Hypothesis: Likely causes include broader/lower-intent audiences, creative/landing mismatch, or UX friction under higher volume.
answer:
Short answer: The data supports all three hypotheses as plausible contributors — cheaper, much higher-volume traffic (likely broader / lower-intent audiences) plus a small drop in conversion that is consistent with creative/landing mismatch or UX friction under higher volume. The period totals: P&L net profit improved to −₹219,593 (from −₹1,185,278) while P&L ad spend rose to ₹708,880 (from ₹293,571) and contribution margin swung to ₹489,287 (from −₹891,706).

What the data shows (1 Oct–13 Oct vs 17 Sep–29 Sep)
- Volume and cost: clicks jumped ~289% (≈1,124 → 4,372/day) and daily ad spend rose ~112% (≈₹25,752 → ₹54,529/day); CPC fell ~50% (₹25.3 → ₹12.6). This is exactly the pattern of much cheaper, higher-volume traffic (consistent with broader / lower-intent audiences).
- Engagement & conversion: CTR rose modestly (2.0% → 2.3%) and add-to-cart rate held steady (2.81% → 2.92%), while conversion rate fell slightly (0.95% → 0.90%). A small drop in conversion with stable/add-to-cart but more clicks is consistent with either a creative→landing mismatch (new traffic not converting) or UX friction when handling higher volume.
- P&L decomposition: higher P&L ad spend reduced profit (effect ≈ −₹451,364) while improved contribution margin increased profit more (effect ≈ +₹1,407,840) — these accounting lines reconcile exactly to the net change. Some ad-level segments (several named ad/adsets in the diagnosis) moved unusually and merit campaign-level review.

Confidence and caveats
- Evidence level: the diagnostics show strong movements in clicks, spend and CPC (measured, high confidence). The assignment of “audience intent” vs “creative/landing mismatch” vs “UX friction” is not proven by totals alone — the data is consistent with all three and suggests where to test them.
- Minor data fetch warnings: a few tax lines failed to fetch but they do not change the decomposition above. Data as of 2026-10-14; the event window ends 2026-10-13.

Worth checking: break down the period by ad platform → campaign → creative (clicks, CPC, CTR, conversion rate, add to cart rate) to see whether the new volume came from specific campaigns/placements (audience change) or from many campaigns at once (site/UX problem).

Period: 2026-10-01..2026-10-13 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-14
